citation: Christoph RA, Buchanan L, Begalla K, Schwartz S. Pain reduction in local anesthetic administration through pH buffering. Ann Emerg Med 1988;17:117-120
found_in_paper: Reference 5 of Todd 1992 (page 726), cited by Todd as the source of the buffering method used for its own lidocaine solutions.
what_it_shows: A randomised, prospective, double-blind study in 25 adult volunteers of three local anaesthetics given by intradermal injection, each plain and each buffered. The third arm was lidocaine with epinephrine at the same anaesthetic and epinephrine strengths C081 attributes to Collins 2013 alone, and onset, extent and duration of skin anaesthesia were all recorded. It is therefore a second independent human intradermal study of that solution with the onset endpoint C081 specifies, which Todd 1992 does not have. The record already cites this paper twice (D025 for its mepivacaine arm, D012 for its pH comparison) without noticing the lidocaine-with-epinephrine arm. Found via Europe PMC; engine: europepmc.
quote_from_abstract: The effects of pH buffering on the pain of administration and efficacy of three local anesthetics ([dose figure omitted] lidocaine, [dose figure omitted] lidocaine with [dose figure omitted] epinephrine, and [dose figure omitted] mepivacaine) were investigated in a randomized, prospective, double-blind study of 25 adult volunteers. ... Onset, extent, and duration of skin anesthesia were not statistically altered by pH buffering.

citation: Swerdlow M, Jones R. The duration of action of bupivacaine, prilocaine and lignocaine. Br J Anaesth 1970;42:335-339
found_in_paper: Reference 4 of Todd 1992 (page 726), cited for previous work on relative duration of action at a single body locale.
what_it_shows: Europe PMC indexes it as a Randomized Controlled Trial and Clinical Trial with MeSH terms Injections, Intradermal; Skin Tests; Epinephrine administration & dosage; Lidocaine; Prilocaine; Pipecolic Acids (bupivacaine); Placebos; Analgesia; and Time Factors, in female subjects. That is a randomised intradermal skin-weal duration study of three anaesthetics with and without adrenaline, which is the paper C039 lists among the seven never opened. No abstract is indexed. It is already the primary paper of another worker in this job (S-686-31, for D009), so it is recorded here only as a reference-list confirmation, not re-judged. Engine: europepmc.

citation: Wightman MA, Vaughan RW. Comparison of compounds used for intradermal anesthesia. Anesthesiology 1976;45:687-689
found_in_paper: Reference 1 of Todd 1992 (page 726), the first of the papers cited for previous single-locale duration work.

It is already the primary paper of another worker in this job (S-686-39, for C038), so it is recorded here only to show that Todd 1992 cites it, which places Todd inside the same intradermal-weal tradition. Not re-judged here.

citation: Gramling ZW, Ellis RG Jr, Volpitto PP. Clinical experiences with mepivacaine (carbocaine). J Med Assoc Ga 1964;53:16-18
what_it_shows: A candidate origin for an old mepivacaine duration figure, but it cannot decide D025. Europe PMC indexes no abstract and no DOI, and its MeSH terms are Mepivacaine, Anesthesia, Anesthesia Conduction, Preanesthetic Medication and Pharmacology, with no intradermal or skin term, so on the indexing available it is a conduction-anaesthesia clinical series rather than a skin-duration measurement. Recorded so the merging session knows it was looked up and found not to be a skin timing study. Engine: europepmc.

citation: Magee C, Rodeheaver GT, Edgerton MT, Golden GT, Haury B, Edlich RF. Studies of the mechanisms by which epinephrine damages tissue defenses. J Surg Res 1977;23:126-131
found_in_paper: Reference 9 of Todd 1992 (page 726), cited at page 725 for epinephrine's vasoconstrictive properties potentiating infection.
what_it_shows: A rabbit study of epinephrine on host defences, indexed under Phagocytosis (drug effects), Immunity (drug effects) and Blood Bactericidal Activity. It measures immune defence rather than nerve or tissue histology, uses a single exposure, and no concentration appears in the indexing, so it neither refutes C075 (repeated infiltration with nerve-fibre counting or nerve histology) nor C093 (tissue damage at a stated dose). It supports the existing reading that the nearest animal work is single-exposure and about wound defence rather than innervation. Engine: europepmc.

citation: Barone JA, Weisman R, Mangione RA, Goldfrank LR. Serum lidocaine concentrations following subcutaneous administration. Clin Pharm 1984;3:281-284
found_in_paper: Reference 12 of Todd 1992 (page 726), cited at page 725 as the contrast to injection through intact skin: lidocaine was undetectable in patients having wounds repaired.
what_it_shows: Thirty patients having lacerations repaired in an emergency department, with venous samples at 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes after subcutaneous lidocaine. The authors conclude that absorption appears altered in traumatised tissue. It is the evidence behind Todd's own caution that wounding may change duration, so it bears on how far any volunteer intact-skin duration figure transfers to wounded tissue, but the claims it would otherwise touch are dose-ceiling claims, which are skipped. Engine: europepmc.
quote_from_abstract: Serum lidocaine concentrations were determined following subcutaneous administration for local anesthesia in the management of lacerations in the emergency room setting.
